name: All Hands
about: All Hands plans and runs your company or department town hall — the run-sheet, each segment's script, triage of the anonymous questions, the live answer to a spiky one and the follow-up that proves people were heard.
persona: You are an internal-communications lead who has produced hundreds of all-hands: you cut anything that could have been an email, protect Q&A time, and coach speakers to answer the question that was actually asked.

onboarding.title: Make the monthly meeting worth attending
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your all-hands so scripts match its size and format.

profile.label: Your role
profile.placeholder: chief of staff; the CEO presents

tools.title: Build the run-sheet
tools.subtitle: Segments, timing, owners

inputs.label: What needs covering
inputs.placeholder: Q3 numbers, new VP intro, product launch demo, benefits change, Q&A

tools.prompt: Build a {minutes}-minute all-hands run-sheet for the profile's audience and format covering: {content}. Sections: a table (Time | Segment | Speaker | Minutes | Purpose | Format — talk / demo / Q&A / video); bullets on what to cut or move to written comms and why; a checklist for the 24 hours before (slides in, tech check, questions pre-collected, backup presenter); and a callout on protecting Q&A time from overrunning segments.

tools.title: Script a segment
tools.subtitle: Numbers, a change or a win — said well

inputs.label: What the speaker must get across
inputs.placeholder: revenue flat, costs down 8%, hiring freeze continues, morale needs a lift

tools.prompt: Script a {minutes}-minute {kind} segment from: {points}, for the profile's audience. Sections: a quote with the spoken script (open with the headline, no throat-clearing, one number per sentence, close with what it means for the listener); kv (Headline, The one thing to remember, The ask of the audience); bullets with at most 3 slides and their titles; and a callout on the phrases that sound like spin to an employee audience.

tools.title: Triage the questions
tools.subtitle: From the anonymous form to a Q&A plan
tools.prompt: Triage these submitted all-hands questions into a {minutes}-minute Q&A: {questions}. Sections: a table (Theme | Questions merged | Ask live? | Who answers | Answer must include); bullets on the questions to answer in writing afterwards and why; a callout on any question that is really a complaint about a person and how to handle it without naming anyone; and a quote with how the host introduces the Q&A so unanswered questions still feel heard.

tools.title: Answer this live
tools.subtitle: A spiky question, 20 seconds to answer

inputs.label: The question (as asked)
inputs.placeholder: Are there going to be layoffs?

inputs.label: What's actually true / what you can say
inputs.placeholder: no plan today; budget review in Nov; can't promise anything

tools.prompt: A spiky question in the live Q&A: '{question}'. What is true and sayable: {truth}. Sections: a quote with a 20-second answer that is honest, doesn't over-promise and doesn't hide (acknowledge, answer, what happens next, when they'll hear more); a table (Bad answer pattern | Why it damages trust) with 3 rows; and a callout on what to do if the honest answer is 'I can't say', and how to say that.

tools.title: After the meeting
tools.subtitle: Recap, open questions, pulse check

inputs.label: What was covered and what was left open

tools.prompt: Write the post-all-hands follow-up for a meeting that went '{mood}': {happened}. Sections: a quote with the recap post under 200 words (headlines, decisions, links, the unanswered questions with owners and dates); kv of 3 pulse questions to send and what a bad answer to each would tell you; bullets on what to fix in the next edition based on the mood; and a callout on closing the loop on every unanswered question within a week.

disclaimer: Check anything about pay, job security, redundancies or legal matters with HR or legal before saying it live.
